title: Field-coefficient compact support is triangulated and preserves lower bounds
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside it [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of quasi-separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For $\Lambda=E$ use the rationalized category $D^b_c(-,E)$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and for $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ use the common finite-stage category $D^b_c(-,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], equipped with the standard bounded t-structures of [prop-constructible-truncations]. The compact-support functor of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] is an exact functor of triangulated categories
$$Rf_!:D^b_c(X,\Lambda)\longrightarrow D^b_c(Y,\Lambda).$$
For every $c\in\mathbf Z$ and $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$,
$$\bigl(\mathcal H^i(K)=0\text{ for all }i<c\bigr)\ \Longrightarrow\ \bigl(\mathcal H^i(Rf_!K)=0\text{ for all }i<c\bigr).$$
Exactness here includes a natural comparison $Rf_!(K[r])\simeq(Rf_!K)[r]$ compatible with distinguished triangles. No separatedness of $X$ or $Y$ over $k$ is assumed.

proof.text: Use the projection-normalized realization of the integral action as exact open extension followed by proper derived image. Pullback is exact on ringed modules, so its derived functor preserves upper bounds. Adjunction orthogonality therefore makes derived image preserve lower bounds. Transport across the realization isomorphism gives the integral lower bound.

Transport the ambient shift comparison through the fully faithful constructible inclusion. The ambient functor is triangulated; reflection along that inclusion gives integral triangulatedness. Apply raw scalar-localization transport to this integral-linear functor. Its objects and tensor Hom maps are definitionally the recorded finite-field functor.

The specified rational standard lower class is the isomorphism closure of integral representatives. Choose such a representative and use the integral bound; map its isomorphism by the rational functor. The common-stage standard lower class is similarly the isomorphism closure of stagewise lower classes. Choose a finite-stage representative and map its isomorphism using the stage-inclusion comparison of the given action.

For a bounded-below object K with cohomology zero below c, start at an existing lower bound a. If a exceeds c, monotonicity suffices. Otherwise induct from a to c. Given K in D^{>=b}, the canonical map tau^{<=b}K to tau^{>=b}tau^{<=b}K is invertible. Vanishing of H^b(K), and faithfulness of shift, make the latter object zero. Thus tau^{<=b}K is zero and K lies in D^{>=b+1}. Conversely a lower bound c makes tau^{<=i}K zero for i<c, hence its cohomology zero. Apply these implications before and after the bounds already proved.

Apply the separate normalized common-stage exactness theorem to S. Combine its coherent integer-shift and triangle preservation with the common-stage lower bound. Combine finite-stage exactness with the finite-stage lower bound, obtaining both conjuncts.

It adds no new node. I read every cited statement and the sources: Bhatt-Scholze Def 6.7.6, Lemma 6.7.7, Remark 6.7.8, Def 6.8.10, Props 6.8.11(3) and 6.8.14, and Stacks 0G2A(3). The statement agrees with them. The mathematics is correct. Steps 1-3 build the integral tower functor, identify it with completed Rp_*j_! (lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison replaces the absent prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits), and transport it rationally. Step 4 compares the framework and PBC pair categories through chi_{L/E} and descends using the cbc coherence on the identity square. Steps 5-7 do the heart bound: the torsion of H is killed by a uniform power of varpi, the Tor transition is multiplication by varpi so the H^{-1} tower is pro-zero, and the Milnor sequence then gives F^int H in D^{>=0} integrally. Steps 8-9 extend this to the rational and Qbar hearts and then by truncation induction. Tested on: K=0, open immersions, A^1->pt, shifts; f=id shows the bound is sharp. Batch-5 flag: lem-cbc-rational-compact-support-coefficient-coherence reaches def-pod-ring-scalar-extension, a general definition of module scalar extension. The cited node states coefficient coherence of compact support, which neither the trace-formula nor the Poincare-duality assumption gives and which is no step of their proofs. So the citation is genuinely outside and I do not return.
